Question 3 [20 marks]: Like a pendulum swinging slow, life requires momentum.
Momentum is movement . . . A force that drives you forward . . .
It’s the beat that prevents you from feeling stuck, that pushes and
propels you towards the life you want to live.
                            Reproduced with permission of Wellbeing Magazine.
Use at least ONE of the ideas in this extract as the basis for an imaginative or discursive piece of writing that explores the need for momentum in our lives.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 20):
17–20 marks: Composes a highly engaging imaginative or discursive piece of writing that effectively uses at least ONE of the ideas in the extract as a basis for the piece | Crafts language skilfully to explore the need for momentum in our lives | Demonstrates highly effective control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and selected form
13–16 marks: Composes an engaging imaginative or discursive piece of writing that effectively uses at least ONE of the ideas in the extract as a basis for the piece | Crafts language effectively to explore the need for momentum in our lives | Demonstrates effective control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and selected form
9–12 marks: Composes an imaginative or discursive piece of writing that uses at least ONE of the ideas in the extract as a basis for the piece | Uses language competently to explore the need for momentum in our lives | Demonstrates sound control of language and structure appropriate to audience, purpose, context and selected form
5–8 marks: Composes a piece of writing that attempts to respond to the question | Demonstrates variable control of language and structure
1–4 marks: Attempts to compose a piece of writing with some relevance to the question Mapping Grid

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award.
